What is Aboji Exercise?

A practice that begins at the center, not at the surface.

Mind · body · one movement

Aboji Exercise is a discipline for restoring the body’s center and bringing mind and body into one coordinated whole. It does not focus on strength or flexibility alone.

Attention, posture, breath, balance, and movement are connected through 丹田. Push and receive. Expand and gather. Tension and release. Opposing actions are coordinated so the whole body can move with continuity.

Not a set of isolated parts, but one body moving from a living center.

Core language of the practice

Some concepts are best kept in their own names.

These terms carry a history and a way of working. We keep their original names, then explain how each one is explored through practice.

01 / CENTER

丹田Dantian · lower center

A practical center for balance, initiation, and whole-body coordination.

02 / CONTINUITY

氣Qi · vital continuity

A traditional body concept explored through attention, breath, and connected movement.

03 / RECIPROCITY

授受JUJU · giving & receiving

Paired actions such as push and receive, rise and sink, working together.

04 / ORIENTATION

中心軸Central axis

The relationship of posture, gravity, rotation, and balance around a stable center.

Principles, felt in movement

The body is the entrance. The deeper we explore, the more we encounter the principles of the universe.

Aboji Exercise uses 丹田, the central axis, breath, and circular, spherical, and spiral movement to connect directions that are often treated separately.

The aim is to sense how attention, posture, and breath meet at the center—and how that center coordinates the body as a whole.

Three dimensions · one centerAttention.
Posture.
Breath.

As these three are brought together through 丹田, movement can extend through the whole body while the center remains present.

01 / LOWER CENTER

丹田 · Dantian

Bring attention to the lower center and let movement begin from there.

02 / CENTRAL AXIS

Stand without forcing

Notice the relationship between the body’s axis and gravity—without forcing a bend or arch.

03 / CIRCULAR & SPHERICAL

Move in more than one plane

Connect front and back, left and right, and up and down through rounded movement.

04 / JUJU

Let opposites cooperate

Coordinate giving and receiving so that opposing forces support one another.

Movement, joined at the center

Two opposing actions become one continuous movement.

Through 授受, the body does not choose one side and discard the other. Both directions are felt, connected, and coordinated around 丹田.

Push & receive

Push ∞ Pull

Expand & gather

Extend ∞ Contract

Tension & release

Engage ∞ Release

From circle to sphere

The spiral brings the whole body into orbit.

圓球 movement brings vertical and horizontal rotations together. Energy turns in a spiral, linking the whole body’s movement with its central axis.

The completion of spiral, spherical movement is the direction toward which Aboji Exercise aims.

Origins · a living transmission

Received through practice. Continued through research. Shared with the next generation.

Aboji Exercise is not only a record of an earlier practice. It is a living effort to receive a movement tradition, examine it in the body, and carry it forward.

c. 1950 · Origins

A bodily discipline takes shape.

Under the extreme conditions of the Heungnam forced-labor camp, Moon Sun-myung developed a disciplined practice of the body and self-mastery.

1995 · Direct transmission

Moon Pyung-rae receives the practice.

The forms of movement were passed on through direct instruction and continued through practice.

2022 · Morning 6 begins

A daily place to practice together.

Online gatherings create a shared rhythm for practice, study, and observation.

Today · Into the future

Research, practice, and transmission.

Participants continue to study the movement through martial arts and East Asian medicine perspectives, and to share it across generations and around the world.

Morning 6 · Daily online practice

When we could not meet in person, we found a way to connect across the world.

One morning.
Many places.
A shared center.

Morning 6 is a daily online gathering to practice Aboji Exercise together at 6:00 a.m. Participants join from different countries and regions, creating a community through steady practice.

On New Year’s Day 2024, 70 people joined the Morning 6 online practice from eight countries.
